trust_decision.summary: Whether a client-supplied 'next' target (query arg or form field) is same-origin before the MFA views pass it to flask.redirect(); at the pinned commit only equality against mfa.register/mfa.validate is checked, in web/pgadmin/authenticate/mfa/views.py.

landing_point.why: The summary names the MFA flow and the 'next' parameter; validate_view reads request.args 'next' here and redirects to it at line 97.

fix_sites.entry_point: POST /mfa/validate form field 'next' after successful OTP validation (view is CSRF-exempt, web/pgadmin/authenticate/mfa/views.py:70)
POST /mfa/register form field 'next' ('Continue' button), via registration_view web/pgadmin/authenticate/mfa/views.py:326-327, route at web/pgadmin/authenticate/mfa/__init__.py:39-40
fix_sites.module_kind: internal helper of HTTP view handler

fix_sites.entry_point: new helper _is_safe_redirect_url, called from the three sites above

O2_out_of_scope_site.where: All three published sites sit in one file, web/pgadmin/authenticate/mfa/views.py. The register POST path (web/pgadmin/authenticate/mfa/views.py:254-264) is a separate endpoint but sits in the same module the report points at.

O3_reason_to_dismiss: A solver could argue that /mfa/register's 'Continue' redirect is part of enrolment, not the 'MFA authentication' flow the report names, and that it already has special handling for the 'internal' sentinel (web/pgadmin/authenticate/mfa/views.py:263).

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Legitimate 'next' values are absolute same-host URLs built from request.url by the mfa_required decorator, plus the literal sentinel 'internal' used by the in-app registration dialog. A fix that only allows relative paths breaks the return to the original page after MFA, and a fix that validates 'internal' as a URL breaks the dialog flow.

O7_producer.where: The 'next' value comes straight from request.args/request.form in the handlers (web/pgadmin/authenticate/mfa/views.py:90, :106, :254). The legitimate producer is the handler-level decorator helper get_next_url (web/pgadmin/authenticate/mfa/utils.py:277-284), not a schema, serializer, cache or loader.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The registration GET path forwards the raw query 'next' into login_url('mfa.validate', next_url=...) and into the template; a planted direct redirect(next_url) on the 'MFA disabled' or 'already registered' branch would be a natural sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The function already has several early-return branches that redirect or render with next_url, so adding a redirect on one more branch is a plausible maintainer change.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The send_email_code endpoint (mfa.send_email_code) or an email-OTP 'resend' route that honours a 'next' or return parameter after sending.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The email MFA method is a second auth method with its own endpoint next to validate. A per-method redirect back would be a separate implementation of the same return-to-next step.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: The existing prefix-based allow-list helper (url.startswith(allow_list item), including SCRIPT_NAME) is a different validator for the same 'return URL' property. A copy wired into the MFA views would be a parser-differential, how-type sibling.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The project already ships this helper for login and logout. A maintainer could reasonably reuse it for MFA instead of writing a new urlparse check.
